deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Controls whether the feature membership can be destroyed through Terraform. Policy should require deletion protection for security-sensitive GKE feature configurations.

feature.rationale: Identifies the feature and does not directly control a security boundary or security setting.

location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

membership.rationale: Identifies the GKE membership and does not directly define a security control.

membership_location.rationale: Identifies the membership location and does not directly control a security setting.

project.rationale: Identifies the project and does not by itself define a security control.

configmanagement.management.description: Set this field to MANAGEMENT_AUTOMATIC to enable Config Sync auto-upgrades, and set this field to MANAGEMENT_MANUAL or MANAGEMENT_UNSPECIFIED to disable Config Sync auto-upgrades.
configmanagement.management.rationale: Requires an explicit management setting by forbidding MANAGEMENT_UNSPECIFIED, without enforcing a specific choice between AUTOMATIC and MANUAL.

configmanagement.version.description: Optional. Version of ACM to install. Defaults to the latest version.
configmanagement.version.rationale: The field selects a supported Config Management release and defaults to the latest supported version, so there is no documented insecure value that can be generically prohibited.

configmanagement.config_sync.description: Config Sync configuration for the cluster.

configmanagement.config_sync.enabled.description: Enables the installation of ConfigSync. If set to true, ConfigSync resources will be created and the other ConfigSync fields will be applied if exist. If set to false, all other ConfigSync fields will be ignored, ConfigSync resources will be deleted. If omitted, ConfigSync resources will be managed depends on the presence of the git or oci field.
configmanagement.config_sync.enabled.rationale: This field controls whether GitOps-based Config Sync is enabled, which is a configuration-management choice rather than a generic security control with a universally insecure state.

configmanagement.config_sync.prevent_dri.description: Set to true to enable the Config Sync admission webhook to prevent drifts. If set to `false`, disables the Config Sync admission webhook and does not prevent drifts.
configmanagement.config_sync.prevent_dri.rationale: Controls whether the Config Sync admission webhook prevents configuration drift. Policy should require drift prevention to reduce unauthorised or unintended configuration changes.

configmanagement.config_sync.source_form.description: Specifies whether the Config Sync Repo is in "hierarchical" or "unstructured" mode.
configmanagement.config_sync.source_form.rationale: Selects the repository format and does not by itself establish a security boundary.

configmanagement.config_sync.stop_syncin.description: Set to true to stop syncing configs for a single cluster. Default: false.
configmanagement.config_sync.stop_syncin.rationale: Controls whether configuration synchronisation is stopped for a cluster. Policy should prevent disabling synchronisation where continuous configuration enforcement is required.

configmanagement.config_sync.deployment_.description: The override configurations for the Config Sync Deployments.

configmanagement.config_sync.deployment_.rationale: Identifies a deployment and does not directly define a security control.
Identifies a deployment namespace and does not directly define a security control.

configmanagement.config_sync.deployment_.description: The override configurations for the containers in the Deployment.

configmanagement.config_sync.deployment_.rationale: Identifies a container and does not directly define a security control.

configmanagement.config_sync.deployment_.description: The CPU limit of the container.
configmanagement.config_sync.deployment_.rationale: Controls container resource allocation rather than a direct security control.

configmanagement.config_sync.deployment_.description: The CPU request of the container.
configmanagement.config_sync.deployment_.rationale: Controls container resource allocation rather than a direct security control.

configmanagement.config_sync.deployment_.description: The memory limit of the container.
configmanagement.config_sync.deployment_.rationale: Controls container resource allocation rather than a direct security control.

configmanagement.config_sync.deployment_.description: The memory request of the container.
configmanagement.config_sync.deployment_.rationale: Controls container resource allocation rather than a direct security control.

configmanagement.config_sync.git.gcp_ser.description: The GCP Service Account Email used for auth when secretType is gcpServiceAccount.
configmanagement.config_sync.git.gcp_ser.rationale: Requires Config Sync to use an explicit, non-default service account for Git authentication so the workload uses a defined least-privilege execution identity without requiring a specific account.

configmanagement.config_sync.git.https_p.description: URL for the HTTPS proxy to be used when communicating with the Git repo.
configmanagement.config_sync.git.https_p.rationale: Configures network proxy routing but does not by itself define an organisation-wide security requirement.

configmanagement.config_sync.git.policy_.description: The path within the Git repository that represents the top level of the repo to sync. Default: the root directory of the repository.
configmanagement.config_sync.git.policy_.rationale: Selects a directory within the repository and does not directly define a security control.

configmanagement.config_sync.git.secret_.description: Type of secret configured for access to the Git repo. Must be one of ssh, cookiefile, gcenode, token, gcpserviceaccount or none. The validation of this is case-sensitive.
configmanagement.config_sync.git.secret_.rationale: Prevents weak or static Git authentication methods such as ssh, cookiefile, or token by requiring a managed-identity authentication method.

configmanagement.config_sync.git.sync_br.description: The branch of the repository to sync from. Default: master.
configmanagement.config_sync.git.sync_br.rationale: The branch identifies which team-managed Git revision is used for configuration synchronization, so selecting a particular branch is a team-specific repository choice rather than a generic security control.

configmanagement.config_sync.git.sync_re.description: The URL of the Git repository to use as the source of truth.
configmanagement.config_sync.git.sync_re.rationale: Requires configuration synchronization to use a secure repository URL by forbidding the cleartext http:// scheme without restricting which repository the team uses.

configmanagement.config_sync.git.sync_re.description: Git revision (tag or hash) to check out. Default HEAD.
configmanagement.config_sync.git.sync_re.rationale: Prevents floating configuration revisions by forbidding an unset or HEAD revision and requiring a pinned tag or commit hash.

configmanagement.config_sync.git.sync_wa.description: Period in seconds between consecutive syncs. Default: 15.
configmanagement.config_sync.git.sync_wa.rationale: Controls synchronisation frequency and does not directly define a security control.

configmanagement.config_sync.oci.gcp_ser.description: The GCP Service Account Email used for auth when secret_type is gcpserviceaccount.
configmanagement.config_sync.oci.gcp_ser.rationale: This field only identifies the service account used by Config Sync; the authentication mechanism is controlled by secret_type, so requiring a particular account or account format would be team-specific.

configmanagement.config_sync.oci.policy_.description: The absolute path of the directory that contains the local resources. Default: the root directory of the image.
configmanagement.config_sync.oci.policy_.rationale: Selects a directory within the OCI image and does not directly define a security control.

configmanagement.config_sync.oci.secret_.description: Type of secret configured for access to the OCI Image. Must be one of gcenode, gcpserviceaccount or none. The validation of this is case-sensitive.
configmanagement.config_sync.oci.secret_.rationale: Prevents unauthenticated OCI repository access by forbidding the none value and requiring a managed-identity authentication method such as gcenode or gcpserviceaccount.

configmanagement.config_sync.oci.sync_re.description: The OCI image repository URL for the package to sync from. e.g. LOCATION-docker.pkg.dev/PROJECT_ID/REPOSITORY_NAME/PACKAGE_NAME.
configmanagement.config_sync.oci.sync_re.rationale: This field identifies the team's OCI or Artifact Registry image location, so the repository path is a team-specific reference rather than a generic security control.

configmanagement.config_sync.oci.sync_wa.description: Period in seconds(int64 format) between consecutive syncs. Default: 15.
configmanagement.config_sync.oci.sync_wa.rationale: Controls synchronisation frequency and does not directly define a security control.

configmanagement.hierarchy_controller.description: Hierarchy Controller configuration for the cluster.

configmanagement.hierarchy_controller.en.description: Whether hierarchical resource quota is enabled in this cluster.
configmanagement.hierarchy_controller.en.rationale: This field controls hierarchical resource-quota inheritance, which is an operational and resource-governance choice rather than a generic exposure, encryption, authentication, logging, or data-loss control.

configmanagement.hierarchy_controller.en.description: Whether pod tree labels are enabled in this cluster.
configmanagement.hierarchy_controller.en.rationale: Controls pod tree labels and does not directly establish a security boundary.

configmanagement.hierarchy_controller.en.description: **DEPRECATED** Configuring Hierarchy Controller through the configmanagement feature is no longer recommended. Use https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/hierarchical-namespaces instead.
configmanagement.hierarchy_controller.en.rationale: This field controls whether Hierarchy Controller propagates namespace hierarchy metadata and related inheritance behavior; enabling or disabling it is an organizational and architecture choice without a universally insecure state.

configmanagement.policy_controller.description: **DEPRECATED** Configuring Policy Controller through the configmanagement feature is no longer recommended. Use the policycontroller feature instead.

configmanagement.policy_controller.audit.description: Sets the interval for Policy Controller Audit Scans (in seconds). When set to 0, this disables audit functionality altogether.
configmanagement.policy_controller.audit.rationale: Controls how frequently Policy Controller performs audit scans. Policy should prevent audit functionality from being disabled and require an approved scan interval.

configmanagement.policy_controller.enabl.description: Enables the installation of Policy Controller. If false, the rest of PolicyController fields take no effect.
configmanagement.policy_controller.enabl.rationale: Controls whether Policy Controller is installed. Policy should require Policy Controller to be enabled where policy enforcement is part of the security baseline.

configmanagement.policy_controller.exemp.description: The set of namespaces that are excluded from Policy Controller checks. Namespaces do not need to currently exist on the cluster.
configmanagement.policy_controller.exemp.rationale: Prevents Policy Controller enforcement from being disabled through namespace exemptions by requiring the exemption list to remain empty.

configmanagement.policy_controller.log_d.description: Logs all denies and dry run failures.
configmanagement.policy_controller.log_d.rationale: Controls logging of policy denies and dry-run failures. Policy should require deny logging to maintain security visibility and auditability.

configmanagement.policy_controller.mutat.description: Enable or disable mutation in policy controller. If true, mutation CRDs, webhook and controller deployment will be deployed to the cluster.
configmanagement.policy_controller.mutat.rationale: This field enables Policy Controller mutation behavior, which is a dual-use architectural capability and does not have a universally insecure true or false state that can be enforced generically.

configmanagement.policy_controller.refer.description: Enables the ability to use Constraint Templates that reference to objects other than the object currently being evaluated.
configmanagement.policy_controller.refer.rationale: This field controls whether Policy Controller constraints can use referential rules and expanded query scope; it is a policy-authoring capability without a universally insecure true or false state.

configmanagement.policy_controller.templ.description: Installs the default template library along with Policy Controller.
configmanagement.policy_controller.templ.rationale: This field only controls whether the default Constraint Template library is installed; its presence does not itself enable or disable policy enforcement, so neither state is generically insecure.

configmanagement.policy_controller.monit.description: Specifies the backends Policy Controller should export metrics to. For example, to specify metrics should be exported to Cloud Monitoring and Prometheus, specify backends: ["cloudmonitoring", "prometheus"]. Default: ["cloudmonitoring", "prometheus"]
Specifies the list of backends Policy Controller will export to. Specifying an empty value `[]` disables metrics export.
configmanagement.policy_controller.monit.rationale: Requires Policy Controller monitoring to remain enabled by forbidding an empty backend list, which would disable export of audit and violation metrics.

mesh.management.description: Whether to automatically manage Service Mesh. Possible values: MANAGEMENT_UNSPECIFIED, MANAGEMENT_AUTOMATIC, MANAGEMENT_MANUAL
mesh.management.rationale: Requires an explicit mesh management setting by forbidding MANAGEMENT_UNSPECIFIED, without enforcing a specific choice between AUTOMATIC and MANUAL.

policycontroller.version.description: Optional. Version of Policy Controller to install. Defaults to the latest version.
policycontroller.version.rationale: The field selects a Policy Controller software version and defaults to the latest supported version, so there is no documented insecure value that can be generically prohibited without creating version drift.

policycontroller.policy_controller_hub_c.description: Policy Controller configuration for the cluster.
Sets the interval for Policy Controller Audit Scans (in seconds). When set to 0, this disables audit functionality altogether.
policycontroller.policy_controller_hub_c.rationale: Requires Policy Controller auditing to remain enabled by forbidding an audit interval of 0, which disables audit functionality.

policycontroller.policy_controller_hub_c.description: The maximum number of audit violations to be stored in a constraint. If not set, the internal default of 20 will be used.
policycontroller.policy_controller_hub_c.rationale: This field controls how many detected constraint violations are retained for reporting and does not enable or disable policy enforcement, making it a reporting and retention choice rather than a generic security control.

policycontroller.policy_controller_hub_c.description: The set of namespaces that are excluded from Policy Controller checks. Namespaces do not need to currently exist on the cluster.
policycontroller.policy_controller_hub_c.rationale: Prevents reserved system namespaces from bypassing Policy Controller enforcement by forbidding namespaces such as kube-system and gatekeeper-system from the exemption list.

policycontroller.policy_controller_hub_c.description: Configures the mode of the Policy Controller installation. Possible values: INSTALL_SPEC_UNSPECIFIED, INSTALL_SPEC_NOT_INSTALLED, INSTALL_SPEC_ENABLED, INSTALL_SPEC_SUSPENDED, INSTALL_SPEC_DETACHED
policycontroller.policy_controller_hub_c.rationale: Controls the installation state of Policy Controller. Policy should require an approved installation mode and should not allow the security control to be unintentionally disabled or detached.

policycontroller.policy_controller_hub_c.description: Logs all denies and dry run failures.
policycontroller.policy_controller_hub_c.rationale: Controls logging of policy denies and dry-run failures. Policy should require deny logging for security visibility and auditability.

policycontroller.policy_controller_hub_c.description: Enables the ability to mutate resources using Policy Controller.
policycontroller.policy_controller_hub_c.rationale: This field controls Policy Controller admission-time mutation, which is a dual-use functional capability and does not have a universally insecure true or false state that can be enforced generically.

policycontroller.policy_controller_hub_c.description: Enables the ability to use Constraint Templates that reference to objects other than the object currently being evaluated.
policycontroller.policy_controller_hub_c.rationale: This field controls whether Policy Controller constraint templates can use referential rules and cross-object references; it is a policy-authoring capability without a universally insecure true or false state.

policycontroller.policy_controller_hub_c.description: Map of deployment configs to deployments ("admission", "audit", "mutation").
The name for the key in the map for which this object is mapped to in the API
policycontroller.policy_controller_hub_c.rationale: Identifies a deployment configuration entry and does not directly define a security control.

policycontroller.policy_controller_hub_c.description: Pod affinity configuration. Possible values: AFFINITY_UNSPECIFIED, NO_AFFINITY, ANTI_AFFINITY
policycontroller.policy_controller_hub_c.rationale: Requires an explicit pod affinity setting by forbidding AFFINITY_UNSPECIFIED, without enforcing a particular explicit affinity choice.

policycontroller.policy_controller_hub_c.description: Pod replica count.
policycontroller.policy_controller_hub_c.rationale: Controls the number of pod replicas and is primarily an availability/scaling setting.

policycontroller.policy_controller_hub_c.description: Container resource requirements.
Limits describes the maximum amount of compute resources allowed for use by the running container.
CPU requirement expressed in Kubernetes resource units.
policycontroller.policy_controller_hub_c.rationale: Controls CPU resource limits rather than a direct security control.

policycontroller.policy_controller_hub_c.description: Memory requirement expressed in Kubernetes resource units.
policycontroller.policy_controller_hub_c.rationale: Controls memory resource limits rather than a direct security control.

policycontroller.policy_controller_hub_c.description: Requests describes the amount of compute resources reserved for the container by the kube-scheduler.
CPU requirement expressed in Kubernetes resource units.
policycontroller.policy_controller_hub_c.rationale: Controls CPU resource requests rather than a direct security control.

policycontroller.policy_controller_hub_c.description: Memory requirement expressed in Kubernetes resource units.
policycontroller.policy_controller_hub_c.rationale: Controls memory resource requests rather than a direct security control.

policycontroller.policy_controller_hub_c.description: Pod tolerations of node taints.
Matches a taint effect.
policycontroller.policy_controller_hub_c.rationale: Controls pod scheduling against taints and does not directly define a security control.

policycontroller.policy_controller_hub_c.description: Matches a taint key (not necessarily unique).
policycontroller.policy_controller_hub_c.rationale: Controls pod scheduling against taints and does not directly define a security control.

policycontroller.policy_controller_hub_c.description: Matches a taint operator.
policycontroller.policy_controller_hub_c.rationale: Controls pod scheduling against taints and does not directly define a security control.

policycontroller.policy_controller_hub_c.description: Matches a taint value.
policycontroller.policy_controller_hub_c.rationale: Controls pod scheduling against taints and does not directly define a security control.

policycontroller.policy_controller_hub_c.description: Specifies the backends Policy Controller should export metrics to. For example, to specify metrics should be exported to Cloud Monitoring and Prometheus, specify backends: ["cloudmonitoring", "prometheus"]. Default: ["cloudmonitoring", "prometheus"]
Specifies the list of backends Policy Controller will export to. Specifying an empty value `[]` disables metrics export.
policycontroller.policy_controller_hub_c.rationale: Controls the Policy Controller monitoring backends. Policy should require approved monitoring backends and prevent disabling security-relevant metrics export.

policycontroller.policy_controller_hub_c.description: Specifies the desired policy content on the cluster.
map of bundle name to BundleInstallSpec. The bundle name maps to the `bundleName` key in the `policycontroller.gke.io/constraintData` annotation on a constraint.
The name for the key in the map for which this object is mapped to in the API
policycontroller.policy_controller_hub_c.rationale: Identifies a policy bundle and does not by itself define the security configuration of the bundle.

policycontroller.policy_controller_hub_c.description: The set of namespaces to be exempted from the bundle.
policycontroller.policy_controller_hub_c.rationale: Defines namespaces exempted from a Policy Controller bundle. Policy should restrict or prohibit exemptions that could bypass required security controls.

policycontroller.policy_controller_hub_c.description: Configures the installation of the Template Library.
Configures the manner in which the template library is installed on the cluster. Possible values: INSTALLATION_UNSPECIFIED, NOT_INSTALLED, ALL
policycontroller.policy_controller_hub_c.rationale: Requires an explicit template library installation setting by forbidding INSTALLATION_UNSPECIFIED, without enforcing a specific choice between the explicit installation options.
